results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Bringer of the Last Gift, Superior Spider-Man and Town Greeter.
results.text:
The deck is submitted as a brew: a Golgari self-mill shell built around Town Greeter, Superior Spider-Man and Bringer of the Last Gift, with a light blue splash for Spider-Man. I considered three directions: Golgari mill (chosen), Dimir midrange with Spider-Man (but Town Greeter is green, so it drops out), and mono-black mill (but Spider-Man needs blue). Golgari was the only one that keeps all three requested cards, and Town Greeter, Overlord of the Balemurk and Molt Tender come from the Golgari Roots shell.

**The plan:** Town Greeter on turn 2 and Overlord of the Balemurk mill the deck toward a graveyard full of creatures. Overlord returns Bringer to hand, Superior Spider-Man copies the best creature in a graveyard, and Bringer at 8 mana wipes both boards and reanimates from both graveyards. Llanowar Elves, Molt Tender and 23 lands get the mana there.

**Honest caveats:**
- The line is slow. On the tool's estimate, every card in the win line is drawn by turn 7 in only about 4% of games.
- Golgari Roots fell from 41 lists in 90 days to 4 in the last 30, and the field is dominated by Izzet Aggro and Vivi Cauldron. Expect to stabilize early and win late.
- Scrapwork Mutt, Haywire Mite and Go for the Throat are not legal in Standard, so I left them out.
- Submit_deck flagged Quag Feast and Coati Scavenger as rarely played. I kept both on purpose, and the submission was accepted with those reasons.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Mightform Harmonizer, Spell Snare and Full Bore.
results.text:
I built a Gruul Landfall brew with a light blue splash for Spell Snare. Mightform Harmonizer is the centerpiece: warp it for 2G, play a land to double its power, then Full Bore (+3/+2, haste, trample on a warp-cast creature) for an 11-damage trample attack on turn 4. Traveling Chocobo makes landfall triggers happen twice, so Harmonizer can reach 16 power. Burn (Burst Lightning, Lightning Strike) and Nova Hellkite cover the rest of the game.

I chose this direction over an Izzet build (Full Bore and Spell Snare, but no Harmonizer) and a three-color Temur build (all three cards, but the mana would be too strained). Izzet is the strongest current shell, but it drops the card you named first. This is a brew, not a proven list. Real decks don't run these three cards together, and Landfall is only 0.8% of the field.

The turn-4 line is fragile. Harmonizer alone is in hand or drawn by turn 4 about 53% of the time, and both Harmonizer and Full Bore by then about 27%. Spell Snare is a single copy because it only counters mana value 2 spells and the blue sources are thin.

results.text:

I weighed three directions: a Rogue-style Temur shell (only 12% of the field, but it can't cast Appa's WW reliably), an Azorius/Esper airbend-control deck (drops Bramble Familiar), and this GW Ally shell, which borrows the Selesnya Offense mana and the Ally package from the menu. I chose GW because all three requested cards fit it and the Ally package makes the Ascension quest counters and Appa's token payoff come online faster.

The plan is to ramp into Appa, Steadfast Guardian at four mana, flash it in, and airbend Airbender Ascension so I can recast it for {2}. Each creature that enters after that adds a quest counter, and Ascension's fourth counter blinks a creature each end step. Ouroboroid and Elspeth, Storm Slayer carry the board from there, with Get Lost, Stroke of Midnight and Airbender's Reversal clearing blockers. The deck is untested: the win line only shows up in about 1.8% of games by turn 5, so this is a starting point, not a proven list. The checker warns about the 19 lands; I kept them because the 6 mana creatures bring the total to 25 mana sources against a low curve.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Abandon Attachments, Firebending Lesson and Combustion Technique.
results.text:
I built a mono-red aggro deck that keeps Izzet Aggro's red core and adds your three Lessons. It's submitted as a brew, with 22 lands and 38 spells.

**Direction chosen:** I considered three options. (1) The Mono-Red firebending list from Standard Challenge 32 (13th place), which is the only real list with your cards but is barely played. (2) Izzet's red creatures and burn with the Lessons added. (3) Boros with white Lessons such as Airbender's Reversal. I chose (2) because Izzet is the most-played deck in the menu, its red cards carry the deck, and it needs no blue, so the Lessons fit without a splash.

**The plan:** Hired Claw, Burnout Bashtronaut and Razorkin Needlehead pressure early. Firebending Lesson, Combustion Technique and Lightning Strike clear blockers, and Burst Lightning adds reach. Abandon Attachments fills the graveyard so Combustion Technique hits harder, and Uncle Iroh makes the Lessons cheaper. Nova Hellkite closes the game.

**Honest caveats:**
- Screaming Nemesis, a staple of Izzet and Boros, is banned in Standard, so I left it out.
- The checker suggests about 24 lands because Izzet runs that many. I used 22 because the deck's average mana value is 1.82, and Claw, Bashtronaut and Burst Lightning give mana sinks. Flooding is the main risk.
- The win line needs every card in it by turn 5 in only 0.3% of games. This deck wins through a steady stream of cheap threats and removal, not that exact sequence.
- The deck has no sideboard, since the task didn't ask for one.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Ashling, Rekindled, Sunderflock and Bounce Off.
results.text:
I built a blue-red Elemental deck around Sunderflock, which is a brew: no published list plays Ashling and Sunderflock together, so it is untested.

**Direction chosen:** I considered three. A Simic Ouroboroid build with Bounce Off would have Sunderflock bouncing its own non-Elemental engine. The Rogue shell that already runs Sunderflock has the same self-bounce problem. So I went blue-red with every creature an Elemental, borrowing Izzet Aggro's burn and mana. That makes Sunderflock's ETB bounce hit only the opponent's board.

**The plan:** Ashling loots early and, when flipped to Rimebound, adds 2 mana for spells costing 4 or more. Flamebraider and Hydro-Man ramp toward a 6–7 drop Elemental such as Eddymurk Crab, Mouth of the Storm, Ice Flan or Shinestriker. That Elemental cuts Sunderflock to around {U}{U}, and its ETB wipes the opponent's non-Elemental creatures while the 5/5 flyer and my board stay. Bounce Off and burn cover the gap until then.

**Honest caveats:**
- The win line (Ashling, Flamebraider, Eddymurk Crab, Sunderflock by turn 7) has all four cards in hand by then only about 3% of the time. Drawing a 6–7 drop Elemental by turn 7 is about 84%, but drawing it together with Sunderflock is only about 43%.
- The checker recommends about 24 lands. I ran 17 and justified it with Flamebraider, Hydro-Man, Ashling and Ice Flan's islandcycling as extra mana.
- Summon: Shiva and Into the Roil are low-played, so I kept them with stated reasons: Shiva is a 5-MV Elemental that cuts Sunderflock's cost, and Into the Roil is instant-speed tempo.

results.prompt: Brew me a Pioneer deck built around Igneous Inspiration, Combustion Technique and Abandon Attachments.
results.text:
The deck is submitted as a brew built on the Izzet Prowess shell, with Igneous Inspiration, Combustion Technique and Abandon Attachments at its center.

**Plan:** Start with cheap prowess creatures (Swiftspear, Soul-Scar Mage, Emberheart Challenger, Screaming Nemesis), use Abandon Attachments to loot toward burn, and clear blockers with Combustion Technique and Reckless Rage. Then finish with Igneous Inspiration to the face. Combustion scales with Lessons in the graveyard, so I added Firebending Lesson, Iroh's Demonstration and Boomerang Basics to feed it.

**Direction chosen:** I considered three. (1) Izzet Prowess with a Lesson package, (2) mono-red Lesson burn, which has too few creatures and card advantage, and (3) Dimir Lesson control, which has few threats. 2. Black-green Survival/Hermit Druid, using mill and discard for graveyard filling. Rejected: it is slower, and Survival of the Fittest is mostly played by Elves.
3. Mono-black Reanimator. Rejected: the black fatties are too thin for Living Death to matter.

**Honest odds:** Living Death alone is in hand by turn 5 in about 57% of games. The full three-card line is drawn by turn 6 in only about 8%, so the deck depends on finding the enablers early. The checker also warned about 15 lands, but the Reanimator list it compares against runs about 14, and Dark Ritual and Lotus Petal cover the rest.

**Things to know:**
- Entomb and Mind Twist are banned in Premodern, and Massacre Wurm, Griselbrand and Barrowgoyf are not legal, so none of them are in the deck.
- Living Death also returns the opponent's graveyard creatures, so check their graveyard before casting it.
- The checker flagged Sickening Dreams as rarely played. I kept it because it is the only card here that fills the graveyard from my own hand and also wipes the opposing board.
